newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Amicable rebuffs Abbey bid.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Amicable rebuffs Abbey bid.

text.p: Life insurance company Scottish Amicable Friday rebuffed a takeover bid worth up to 1.4 billion pounds ($2.3 billion) from British retail banking group Abbey National Plc.
Scottish Amicable said it would pursue its own plan, announced earlier this month, to shed its mutual ownership status and seek a stock market flotation in three to five years.

"We believe this offer will by very attractive to Scottish Amicable policyholders, providing them with immediate value and the long-term security of being part of one of the UK's strongest financial groups," Abbey National Chief Executive Peter Birch said in a statement.

The Abbey offer, which surprised the market, includes a minimum of 400 million pounds ($648 million) to policyholders in cash or Abbey shares and an immediate investment of between 700 million ($1.1 billion) to one billion pounds ($1.6 billion).

Despite the rejection by Scottish Amicable, the Abbey, Britain's fifth-largest bank, said it still hoped to persuade Scottish Amicable, which has 14 billion pounds ($22.7 billion) under management, to accept the offer and put it to its policy-holders.

"We feel that we can offer something much more attractive to the Scottish Amicable policy holders," Abbey deputy chief executive Charles Toner said. "That's why we really want to talk to Scottish Amicable and we hope still to persuade them to put this more attractive deal to their policy holders."

Under the second element of the offer, Abbey National would invest between 700 million ($1.1 billion) and one billion pounds ($1.6 billion) into a Scottish Amicable fund in which the policyholder is entitled to a share of the profits from the growth of the fund.

Scottish Amicable said it intends to publish in 10 days detailed proposals about a twin-phased transformation involving losing its mutual status on May 1 and a 1.0 billion pound ($1.6 billion) stock flotation.
